options.label: Accept now (Recommended)
options.description: Status becomes 'Accepted, 2026-10-27, by the maintainer' in this round's fix pass. Every citing line becomes true, matching how RFC-0026 was handled.

options.label: Accept at merge
options.description: Keep Under Review for now. I flip the status in the last fix pass, after the review loop converges. Until then the finding stays open.

options.label: Mark lines pending
options.description: Keep the RFC Under Review. The RFC-0024/0026 lines, the register row and the BACKLOG-DONE moves are marked pending ([~]). That is more churn and blocks /observe OP-01 until it is accepted.

questions.question: shared.md joins the ground without a formal model because it 'holds definitions only', but its Handle, Lifetime and State sections are meant to get clauses later. What happens when a flow fills a section?

options.label: Clause joins under R1 (Recommended)
options.description: State in RFC-0027 P2, the register and shared.md: the exemption covers definitions only. A clause written into a section joins the ground as any clause does under R1, with its flow's spec and model accepted. Until then the section holds no clause. This keeps your 'bare skeleton, filled after each session' cut.

options.label: Pointer only
options.description: shared.md never holds clauses. A filled section defines its subject and points to the spec or model that holds the clause, so the exemption stays true forever. The file becomes a routing index, not a home.

options.label: Exemption covers clauses
options.description: State that shared.md's clauses join without a model too. That is the smallest edit, but it widens RFC-0024 R1, since unmodelled clauses become ground.
